newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 6.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Wesfarmers on Tuesday reported an annual net profit of A$139.55 million and increased its final dividend to 38 cents from 20 cents. Analysts had expected a pre-abnormals net profit of about A$135 million and brokers also welcomed the higher dividend. However, Wesfarmers Managing Director Michael said he expected the pace of growth in the current financial year to slow.
Pacific BBA released its first half earnings on Tuesday, posting a 27 percent rise to A$12.6 million.

The A$2.3 billion merger of Australian nickel producer QNI Ltd with Gencor Ltd's Billiton Nickel looks set to gain grudging shareholder approval after the deal was sweetened on Tuesday, analysts said. QNI announced revised terms for the merger, reducing the number of shares to be issued to Billiton Nickel to 455.802 million shares (52.5 percent of the enlarged QNI) from 504.03 million (55 percent) and raising a planned capital return to 30 cents a share from 28 cents.

The federal government agreed with the state governments to impose a whole new set of national taxes on tobacco, petrol and alcohol to replace those state taxes struck down by the High Court on Tuesday. The Financial Review said officials believe cigarette prices could rise in some states because of the new regime.

Henry Walker posted an 18 percent rise in net profit for the year to A$20.99 million and increased its final dividend to 4.75 cents per share from 4.5 cents per share. It also said it was targeting further growth in the year.

Broadcaster Prime Television Ltd said on Wednesday it had raised A$21.09 million through a placement of 7.4 million shares at A$2.85 a share to fund recent and future expansion. Prime also said it expected net profit for the year to June 30, 1997 to be at the high end of market expectations of A$15.5 million to A$16.0 million.
